questions.q: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\cos^2\left(\cot^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{2+x}{2-x}}\right)\right]$ is
questions.explanation: Put $x=2\cos\theta$; then $\dfrac{2+x}{2-x}=\cot^2\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, so $\cos^2\left(\cot^{-1}\sqrt{\cdot}\right)=\cos^2\dfrac{\theta}{2}=\dfrac12+\dfrac{x}{4}$. Differentiating gives $\dfrac14$.

questions.q: For the function $f(x)=x^3-6x^2+12x-3$; $x=2$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=3x^2-12x+12$ so $f'(2)=0$; $f''(x)=6x-12$ so $f''(2)=0$; $f'''(2)=6\neq0$, hence $x=2$ is a point of inflexion.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=|\cos x|$ is
options: Everywhere continuous but not differentiable at odd multiples of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
Neither continuous nor differentiable at $(2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}, n\in Z$
questions.explanation: $|\cos x|$ is continuous everywhere but has sharp corners wherever $\cos x=0$, i.e. at odd multiples of $\pi/2$, where it fails to be differentiable.

questions.q: If $y=2x^{3x}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x=1$ is
questions.explanation: $\log y=\log 2+3x\log x \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3(\log x+1)$. At $x=1$, $y=2$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2\times3(0+1)=6$.

questions.q: Let the function satisfy the equation $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in R$, where $f(0)\neq 0$. If $f(5)=3$ and $f'(0)=2$, then $f'(5)$ is
questions.explanation: Such a function is exponential, $f(x)=a^x$, so $f'(x)=f(x)f'(0)$ for all $x$ (differentiating the functional equation w.r.t. $y$ at $y=0$). Hence $f'(5)=f(5)\cdot f'(0)=3\times2=6$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{x\left[6(\log x)^2+7\log x+2\right]}dx=$
questions.explanation: Put $\log x=t$ so $\dfrac{1}{x}dx=dt$. $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{(3t+2)(2t+1)}=\int\left(\dfrac{-3}{3t+2}+\dfrac{2}{2t+1}\right)dt=\log\left|\dfrac{2t+1}{3t+2}\right|+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin\dfrac{5x}{2}}{\sin\dfrac{x}{2}}dx=$
questions.explanation: $\sin\dfrac{5x}{2}=\sin\dfrac{x}{2}\left(3-4\sin^2 x\right)+2\cos x\sin\dfrac{x}{2}$ type expansion reduces the integrand to $1+2\cos 2x+2\cos x$, which integrates to $x+2\sin x+\sin 2x+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_1^5\left(|x-3|+|1-x|\right)dx=$
questions.explanation: For $x\in[1,3]$ the integrand is $2$, and for $x\in[3,5]$ it is $2x-4$. So the integral $=2(2)+\left[x^2-4x\right]_3^5=4+8=12$.

questions.q: If lines $\dfrac{x-1}{-3}=\dfrac{y-2}{2k}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x-1}{3k}=\dfrac{y-5}{1}=\dfrac{z-6}{-5}$ are mutually perpendicular, then $k$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Perpendicularity gives $(-3)(3k)+(2k)(1)+(2)(-5)=0 \Rightarrow -9k+2k-10=0 \Rightarrow k=-\dfrac{10}{7}$.

questions.q: Corner points of the feasible region for an LPP are (0, 2), (3,0), (6, 0), (6, 8) and (0, 5). Let $z=4x+6y$ be the objective function. The minimum value of $z$ occurs at
options: The mid-point of the line segment joining the points (0, 2) and (3, 0)
Any point on the line segment joining the points (0, 2) and (3, 0)
questions.explanation: $z(0,2)=12$ and $z(3,0)=12$ are equal, so the line $z=12$ is parallel to the edge joining these two corner points; the minimum is attained at every point of that segment.

If in two circles, arcs of the same length subtend angles $30^0$ and $78^0$ at the centre, then the ratio of their radii is
questions.explanation: Equal arc length gives $r_1\theta_1=r_2\theta_2$, so $\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}=\dfrac{\theta_2}{\theta_1}=\dfrac{78}{30}=\dfrac{13}{5}$.

questions.q: If $\triangle ABC$ is right angled at $C$, then the value of $\tan A+\tan B$ is
questions.explanation: With the right angle at $C$, $\tan A=\dfrac{a}{b}$ and $\tan B=\dfrac{b}{a}$, so $\tan A+\tan B=\dfrac{a^2+b^2}{ab}=\dfrac{c^2}{ab}$ by Pythagoras.

questions.q: The real value of '$\alpha$' for which $\dfrac{1-i\sin\alpha}{1+2i\sin\alpha}$ is purely real is
questions.explanation: Rationalising, the imaginary part is proportional to $-3\sin\alpha$. For this to vanish, $\sin\alpha=0$, i.e. $\alpha=n\pi,n\in N$.

questions.q: The length of a rectangle is five times the breadth. If the minimum perimeter of the rectangle is 180 cm, then

questions.q: In the expansion of $(1+x)^n$, $\dfrac{C_1}{C_0}+2\dfrac{C_2}{C_1}+3\dfrac{C_3}{C_2}+\dots+n\dfrac{C_n}{C_{n-1}}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since $\dfrac{C_r}{C_{r-1}}=\dfrac{n-r+1}{r}$, the $r$-th term $r\cdot\dfrac{C_r}{C_{r-1}}=n-r+1$. Summing $r=1$ to $n$ gives $n+(n-1)+\dots+1=\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$.

questions.q: The angle between the line $x+y=3$ and the line joining the points $(1,1)$ and $(-3,4)$ is
questions.explanation: Slope of $x+y=3$ is $m_1=-1$; slope of the joining line is $m_2=-\dfrac{3}{4}$. $\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1m_2}\right|=\dfrac{1}{7}$.

questions.q: The equation of parabola whose focus is $(6,0)$ and directrix is $x=-6$ is
questions.explanation: With focus $(a,0)=(6,0)$, the parabola $y^2=4ax$ gives $y^2=24x$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\frac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{\sqrt2\cos x-1}{\cot x-1}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: By L'Hopital's rule, the limit reduces to $\dfrac{-\sqrt2\sin x}{-\csc^2x}$ at $x=\pi/4$, giving $\sqrt2\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac12$.

questions.q: The negation of the statement "For every real number x; $x^2+5$ is positive" is
options: For every real number x; $x^2+5$ is not positive.
For every real number x; $x^2+5$ is negative
There exists at least one real number x such that $x^2+5$ is not positive
There exists at least one real number x such that $x^2+5$ is positive
questions.explanation: The negation of a universal statement "for every x, P(x)" is the existential statement "there exists x such that not P(x)".

questions.q: Let a, b, c, d and e be the observations with mean m and standard deviation S. The standard deviation of the observations $a+k,b+k,c+k,d+k$ and $e+k$ is
questions.explanation: Adding the same constant $k$ to every observation shifts the mean by $k$ but does not change the spread, so the standard deviation stays $S$.

questions.q: Let $f:R\to R$ be defined by $f(x)=x^2+1$. Then the pre images of 17 and -3 respectively are
questions.explanation: $x^2+1=17\Rightarrow x=\pm4$. $x^2+1=-3$ has no real solution since $x^2+1\ge1$, so its preimage is $\phi$.

questions.q: Let $(gof)(x)=\sin x$ and $(fog)(x)=(\sin\sqrt x)^2$. Then
questions.explanation: Try $f(x)=\sin^2x,g(x)=\sqrt x$: $g(f(x))=\sqrt{\sin^2x}=\sin x$ and $f(g(x))=\sin^2\sqrt x=(\sin\sqrt x)^2$, matching both given compositions.

questions.q: Let $A=\{2,3,4,5,\dots,16,17,18\}$. Let R be the relation on the set A of ordered pairs of positive integers defined by $(a,b)R(c,d)$ if and only if $ad=bc$ for all $(a,b),(c,d)$ in $A\times A$. Then the number of ordered pairs of the equivalence class of $(8,2)$ is
questions.explanation: $(a,b)R(8,2)$ means $2a=8b$, i.e. $a=4b$. Pairs in $A\times A$ satisfying this are $(8,2),(12,3),(16,4)$ and their "reverses" from the relation's symmetry, giving 6 ordered pairs: $\{(3,2),(6,4),(9,6),(12,8),(18,12),(15,10)\}$ type listing as per the key.

questions.q: If $\cos^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}y+\cos^{-1}z=3\pi$, then $x(y+z)+y(z+x)+z(x+y)$ equal
questions.explanation: Since each $\cos^{-1}$ term is at most $\pi$, the sum $3\pi$ forces $x=y=z=-1$. Then $x(y+z)+y(z+x)+z(x+y)=2(xy+yz+zx)=2(3)=6$.

questions.q: If A is square matrix such that $A^2=A$, then $(I+A)^3$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $(I+A)^3=I+3A+3A^2+A^3$. Since $A^2=A$ (and hence $A^3=A$), this equals $I+3A+3A+A=I+7A$.

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\begin{vmatrix}\cos x&x&1\\2\sin x&x&2x\\sin x&x&x\end{vmatrix}$. Then $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{f(x)}{x^2}=$
questions.explanation: Expanding the determinant gives $f(x)=-x^2\cos x+x\sin x$, so $\dfrac{f(x)}{x^2}=-\cos x+\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\to -1+1=0$ as $x\to0$.

questions.q: Which one of the following observations is correct for the features of logarithm function to base b>1?
options: The domain of the logarithm function is R, the set of real numbers
The range of the logarithm function is $R^+$, the set of all positive real numbers.
The point (1,0) is always on the graph of the logarithm function
The graph of the logarithm function is decreasing as we move from left to right.
questions.explanation: Since $\log_b1=0$ for any base $b>1$, the point $(1,0)$ always lies on the graph of the logarithm function.

questions.q: If $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&\alpha&3\\1&3&3\\2&4&4\end{pmatrix}$ is the adjoint of a $3\times3$ matrix A and $|A|=4$, then $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $|P|=|A|^{n-1}=|A|^2=16$. Evaluating $|P|$ in terms of $\alpha$ gives $2\alpha-6=16$, so $\alpha=11$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{vmatrix}x&1\\1&x\end{vmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{vmatrix}x&1&1\\1&x&1\\1&1&x\end{vmatrix}$, then $\dfrac{dB}{dx}$ is
questions.explanation: $A=x^2-1$. Expanding $B$ gives $B=(x+2)(x-1)^2$, and differentiating and simplifying yields $\dfrac{dB}{dx}=3(x^2-1)=3A$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=xe^{x(1-x)}$ then $f(x)$ is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=e^{x-x^2}(1+x-2x^2)$. Since $e^{x-x^2}>0$, the sign is that of $1+x-2x^2=-(2x+1)(x-1)$, which is $\ge0$ for $x\in[-1/2,1]$; hence $f$ is increasing there.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sin x}{3+4\cos^2x}dx=$
questions.explanation: Put $\cos x=t$, $-\sin x\,dx=dt$: $-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{3+4t^2}=-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2t}{\sqrt3}\right)+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}(1-x^2)\sin x\cdot\cos^2x\,dx=$
questions.explanation: The integrand $(1-x^2)\sin x\cos^2x$ is an odd function of $x$ (even $\times$ odd $\times$ even), so its integral over the symmetric interval $[-\pi,\pi]$ is 0.

questions.q: The function $x^x; x>0$ is strictly increasing at
questions.explanation: For $f(x)=x^x$, $f'(x)=x^x(1+\log x)$, which is positive when $1+\log x>0$, i.e. $x>\dfrac1e$.

questions.q: The maximum volume of the right circular cone with slant height 6 units is
questions.explanation: With $l^2=r^2+h^2=36$, $V=\dfrac{\pi}{3}(36-h^2)h$. Maximising gives $h^2=12,r^2=24$, so $V_{max}=16\sqrt3\pi$ cubic units.

questions.q: The vectors $\vec{AB}=3\hat i+4\hat k$ and $\vec{AC}=5\hat i-2\hat j+4\hat k$ are the sides of a $\triangle ABC$. The length of the median through A is
questions.explanation: The median from A is $\dfrac12(\vec{AB}+\vec{AC})=\dfrac12(8\hat i-2\hat j+8\hat k)=4\hat i-\hat j+4\hat k$, with length $\sqrt{16+1+16}=\sqrt{33}$.

questions.q: Let $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ be two unit vectors and $\theta$ is the angle between them. Then $\vec a+\vec b$ is a unit vector if
questions.explanation: $|\vec a+\vec b|^2=1+1+2\cos\theta=1 \Rightarrow \cos\theta=-\dfrac12 \Rightarrow \theta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

questions.q: The solution of $e^{\frac{dy}{dx}}=x+1, y(0)=3$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\log(x+1) \Rightarrow y=(x+1)\log(x+1)-(x+1)+C$. Using $y(0)=3$ gives $C=4$, which rearranges to $y+x-3=(x+1)\log(x+1)$.

questions.q: The family of curves whose x and y intercepts of a tangent at any point are respectively double the x and y coordinates of that point is
questions.explanation: If the tangent at $(x_1,y_1)$ has intercepts $2x_1,2y_1$, its equation gives the differential equation $x\,dy+y\,dx=0$ whose solution is $xy=C$.
